text:
T.J. Hughes took the long road here. Never drafted, he scored 57 points in 40 games at Michigan last season, signed as a free agent and has played all 23 of Colorado's games as a rookie, on about 15 minutes a night with time on the power play. The Colorado Springs Gazette is already writing about how he sticks long-term.

The scoring line says 2 goals and 11 points. The chances say more. He has 6.1 expected goals, more than 1 per 60 minutes, and he's gone 14 games without a goal on 4.1 expected. Shooting under 4% isn't who anyone is; goals tend to follow chances, and he keeps getting them. Meanwhile he's been feeding others, with seven assists in his last ten games.

The caution is defensive. Colorado's share of expected goals falls about six points when he's on at five on five compared with when he sits, so the line is giving back some of what it creates. We'd watch whether the finishing arrives before the coaching staff starts thinking about the other end.
